skills.name: Causes of the Second World War

note.text: The Second World War had interacting causes. Nazi expansionism sought conquest and racial domination; explaining it does not endorse it. Resentment over the postwar settlement and the economic crisis helped destabilise politics, but did not make war inevitable. The League of Nations failed to check major aggression effectively. Appeasement sought to avoid another war through concessions; Munich did not stop Hitler. Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939; Britain and France declared war on 3 September. This marks the conventional European outbreak, while war in Asia had earlier roots.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish underlying causes from the immediate European trigger and explain how aggression and failed restraint interacted. Builds on: Form Three’s imperial rivalry, the First World War and its settlement. Leads to: Cameroon’s involvement in a war fought through imperial networks.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: The Second World War had interacting causes. Nazi expansionism sought conquest and racial domination; explaining it does not endorse it. Resentment over the postwar settlement and the economic crisis helped destabilise politics, but did not make war inevitable. The League of Nations failed to check major aggression effectively. Appeasement sought to avoid another war through concessions; Munich did not stop Hitler. Germany invaded Poland on {1} September {1939}; Britain and France declared war on {3} September. This marks the conventional European outbreak, while war in Asia had earlier roots.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: Compare stages: Japanese expansion in Manchuria from {1931}, Italy’s invasion of Ethiopia in {1935}, German remilitarisation of the Rhineland in {1936}, and Munich in {1938}. German occupation of the Czech lands in March {1939} undermined further promises of restraint. The German-Soviet non-aggression pact in August {1939} reduced Hitler’s immediate fear of a two-front war; it did not create a permanent alliance. The Soviet Union also invaded Poland later that September. Different crises weakened the international order before the invasion that triggered the wider European war.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Build an explanation rather than a list: identify a condition, explain how it enabled aggression, then connect it to a decision. Distinguish motives, failed responses and the trigger. Compare diplomatic promises with subsequent actions. A contemporary speech reveals its speaker’s position; it does not prove that every citizen agreed or that a promised peace occurred.

cards.idea: Distinguish the historical features before explaining their relationship.
example: expansionism: a policy seeking territorial conquest and domination.
appeasement: concessions intended to avoid war with an aggressive power.
failure of collective security: the inability of international cooperation to restrain major aggression effectively.
economic instability: hardship that increased political tensions without making aggression inevitable.
immediate European trigger: Germany’s invasion of Poland leading to British and French declarations of war.

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.
example: Nazi leaders pursued an empire in eastern Europe and used force against neighbouring states.
At Munich in {1938}, concessions over the Sudetenland were accepted in the hope of avoiding war.
The League failed to prevent Italy’s conquest of Ethiopia despite the principle of collective restraint.
Depression damaged livelihoods and helped extremist parties exploit fear and resentment.
Germany attacked Poland on {1} September {1939}; Britain and France declared war on {3} September.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Nazi expansion was simply a peaceful request with no conquest aim. Correction: Expansionist policy involved deliberate conquest; economic hardship alone did not force that choice.
The Munich settlement permanently ended German expansion. Correction: The later occupation of Czech lands and invasion of Poland show that Munich did not prevent further aggression.
The League successfully prevented every invasion in the interwar period. Correction: Its ineffective response to major aggression weakened confidence in collective security.
Every country experiencing depression necessarily chose aggressive war. Correction: Economic crisis created pressures; political choices and different national circumstances still mattered.
The invasion of Poland happened after Britain’s September declaration of war. Correction: The invasion preceded those declarations; distinguish the immediate sequence from deeper causes.
